independence_declaration.statement: I (code-security-reviewer, session 38ae0562) authored none of the DG1 implementation or the round-11 repairs. Those are d54c151 (T-DG1-FE3 frontend-ux-engineer, T-DG1-BE12 backend-workflow-engineer) and 7c3ebb2 (orchestrator, D-055 wording). I reported F-DG1-132 in round 10 and verify it here as its originating reviewer. At start the real-repo HEAD was d8eb695, one commit past the freeze commit 32e6478, and that commit adds only candidate-excluded metadata (round-11 assignments, manifest, stages.json). The recomputed ID is e5cc6ef9 at both commits, in the real repo and in a full disposable clone. During my run HEAD advanced to d58454c, the runner's auto-commit of the domain reviewer's round-11 run. I checked only its file NAMES (reviews/DG1/round-11/domain-reviewer.* and runs/), and the ID is still e5cc6ef9. I formed this verdict before, and without, reading any other reviewer's round-11 record. I did not open any of them.

The ID is e5cc6ef982ba...feb8 (391 files) in the real repo, in the clone at 32e6478 and at d8eb695, and again after HEAD advanced to d58454c (another reviewer's auto-commit, records and runs only). The source delta is architecture.test.ts, architecture.testkit.ts, apps/web/test/jsdom-native-abort-environment.ts (new), apps/web/tsconfig.json and apps/web/vitest.config.ts. Manifest entries: +1 added (the harness file), 5 changed (those four plus decisions.md, D-055 / F-DG1-011), 0 removed.

checks_run.procedure: Plant probes through fileViolations('transformations', …/zz-planted.ts) in the clone: 16 spelled and computed setEngine forms (must flag), 5 enumeration forms (E1-E4 as pinned, plus E5 dynamic import() then enumerate; documented residual (a), must NOT flag), 3 positive controls (must be clean). Also check the real 13-module tree (moduleViolations), and scan every module file for namespace, default, dynamic or export* use of node:crypto (is a narrow closure feasible?). Run on Node 22 and Node 24 together with architecture.test.ts.
checks_run.command: npx vitest run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-r11-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts (the probe is a temporary file in the clone; copy at zz-r11-probe.test.ts.txt)
checks_run.environment: disposable clone @d8eb695; node v22.22.2 and v24.21.0
checks_run.expected: Spelled forms 16/16 flagged; E1-E5 give 0 violations; positives clean; real tree 0; architecture.test.ts about 109/109
checks_run.actual: On both runtimes: SPELLED 16/16 flagged ('native loader via … setEngine', with rule 2 for the concatenated and computed-destructuring keys). ENUM E1-E5 n=0 (residual (a), as documented). POSITIVE P1-P3 n=0. REAL-TREE 13 modules, 0 violations. architecture.test.ts 109/109. 135/135 total with the probe. NARROW-CLOSURE scan: 41 module files, no namespace, default, dynamic or export* use of node:crypto. So a named-imports-only rule for node:crypto would close E1-E5 without breaking current code, and the header's 'not closable statically / would break identity/access' justification is inaccurate (F-DG1-133, Low). The first two probe runs had harness defects of mine (API_MODULES is an object, and moduleFiles returns relative paths). Both are logged and corrected; the final runs exit 0.

checks_run.procedure: Read the testkit header, the E-case comment and D-055, and check the identity and access call sites they cite as the reason a namespace-as-value ban is not viable.
checks_run.command: grep -n 'Object.entries\|new Map(' apps/api/src/modules/identity apps/api/src/modules/access; sed -n 63,80p apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; sed -n 530,535p apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts
checks_run.expected: The cited code uses a module namespace as a value, so a namespace ban would break it, or the framing is otherwise accurate
checks_run.actual: identity/routes.ts:35 `new Map(Object.entries(request.cookies)).get(name)` and access/rules.ts:55 `new Map(Object.entries(PERMISSIONS))` enumerate plain objects, not a namespace. A blanket ban on dynamic reads would break them; a namespace-as-value ban for node:crypto would not. 'Every SPELLED form' is now accurate and the reach is honestly named. Only the 'not closable statically' and 'would break' rationale (testkit.ts:63, :72-74; test.ts:533) overstates the cost. Raised as F-DG1-133 (Low, non-mandatory).

checks_run.procedure: Confirm the F-DG1-214 change is confined to the web test harness and is not shipped. Review the environment code. Probe the custom env on Node 24 and Node 22: Request accepts the global AbortController's signal, abort propagates, and the jsdom document and window are present. Negative control: revert environment to the built-in 'jsdom' (disposable edit) and run unit-web on Node 24. Grep the built web dist and the deploy files for the harness.
checks_run.command: git diff --name-only 265af7e 32e6478 -- apps/web; npx vitest run --project unit-web (with a temporary probe, then with environment: "jsdom"); grep -rl 'jsdom-native-abort|ABORT_GLOBALS' apps/web/dist; grep -rn apps/web/test deploy Dockerfile*
checks_run.environment: disposable clone @d8eb695; node v24.21.0 and v22.22.2
checks_run.expected: Only apps/web/test/jsdom-native-abort-environment.ts, vitest.config.ts and tsconfig.json change, with no product or runtime file; the fix makes unit-web green on Node 24; the built-in env reproduces the failure; the harness is absent from the build
checks_run.actual: The web delta is exactly the 3 harness files, and no apps/web/src, api, worker or package file changed. The env captures the global AbortController/AbortSignal descriptors before jsdom setup and redefines them after it. Nothing else changes, and it is a dev-only import of vitest/environments. Probe: 111/111 on Node 24 and on Node 22. The signal is accepted by Request and abort propagates; AbortSignal is Node's class (lib/internal/abort_controller.js); document and window are present. (My first probe variant asserted '[native code]', a wrong premise for Node's JS-implemented class. Logged and corrected.) Negative control with the built-in 'jsdom' on Node 24: 13 failed / 98 passed with 'RequestInit: Expected signal ("AbortSignal {}") to be an instance of AbortSignal', the round-10 defect, so the harness fix is what turns it green. The harness string is not in apps/web/dist, and no deploy file references apps/web/test. Product code passes signals only to fetch (api/client.ts), never to DOM addEventListener, so a realm mismatch with jsdom's EventTarget is not exercised. Runtime behaviour on Node 24 is QA's to verify; I did not close F-DG1-214.

summary: PASS. F-DG1-132 is verified as an accepted observation, and F-DG1-215 receives the same specialist acceptance (both need the auditor's acceptance too). Rule 1 flags 16/16 spelled and computed setEngine forms on Node 22 and Node 24. Enumeration (E1-E5) is the documented residual (a). Positive controls are clean, the real tree has 0 violations and architecture.test.ts passes 109/109. F-DG1-214 is confirmed harness-only: 3 web test-harness files, nothing shipped. The negative control reproduces the round-10 Node-24 failure with the built-in jsdom env, and the custom env makes unit-web green on both runtimes (302/302 unit on Node 22 and on Node 24). All required checks pass: integration 200/200 twice on Node 22 plus once on Node 24, gates/agents 105, deploy 59, install-sandbox 13/13 registry-free cases, SBOM, DG0 historical, ci.yml x3 identical. AC-1 (effect) and a real-repo install are BLOCKED (no registry). New finding F-DG1-133 (Low, non-mandatory): the residual (a) rationale wrongly calls the node:crypto namespace route statically unclosable and cites identity/access code that a narrow ban would not affect. No Critical, High or mandatory finding is unresolved from my review.
